$comment: FRW-BL-107 — the platform tool registry the hook-config auditor reads.
WHY THIS IS DATA AND NOT CODE: the auditor needs to know which tool names exist, which share a
capability class, and which input fields each one sends. That set changes with platform versions.
A hardcoded list inside the linter rots into false positives, which is how a linter gets disabled
(the card's own technicalNotes say exactly this). Keeping it as versioned data means a platform
update is a one-file diff with a visible provenance stamp, not a code change.
SCOPE, deliberately narrow: the tools Volundr actually matches on, plus their known capability
siblings. Universal coverage is NOT attempted — an incomplete map that pretends to be complete
would produce confident wrong answers. Anything not listed here is UNKNOWN, and the auditor warns
rather than blocks on unknown names (ISC-6), so a new platform tool cannot wedge the gate suite.
PROVENANCE: field lists were read off the live tool schemas available to the lead in session
12811400 (2026-08-12) on CLI 2.1.228, cross-checked against the fields Volundr's own hooks
actually read. They are the fields relevant to hook guards, not exhaustive tool signatures.

capabilityClasses.shell: Executes a command through a shell. A guard for one of these must guard all of them — FRW-BL-092 was exactly this defect (Bash guarded, PowerShell and Monitor unguarded and invisible).
capabilityClasses.file-write: Mutates a file on disk. FRW-BL-093 was this defect (Write and Edit guarded, NotebookEdit unguarded).
capabilityClasses.spawn: Starts a subagent. Attribution and dependency guards keyed to one of these miss the others — FRW-BL-094 tracks the Workflow half.
capabilityClasses.skill: Loads instructions into the session. Not a mutation class, but Volundr guards tool-priority here.
capabilityClasses.read: Reads without mutating. No guard obligation; listed so the auditor recognises the names.

waivers.reason: Documented deferral, not an oversight. Adding Workflow to the Agent matcher would feed a workflow SCRIPT to enforce-card-deps.js, which expects a single-card Agent prompt, and would not touch the positional-pop defect that is the real bug. Recorded in framework/hook-coverage.md under 'The Workflow attribution gap - deferred, with the reason'. Present exposure in this repo is nil: the standing instruction here is not to use the Workflow tool.

$waiverPolicy: A waiver MUST name a card. That is the same bar framework/hook-coverage.md sets for its coverage table ('no row reads GAP without either a card reference or a recorded deferral') — a gap someone decided to accept is fine; an undocumented one is not. The auditor reports every applied waiver in its output so an accepted gap stays visible instead of becoming invisible.
